You do not know anything about the reasons, causes of the operations; you were not familiar with it because you were not part of the structures?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I don't know anything about the details; I just know about the consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing. You also spoke about the arrival of the Mice Group, about their arrest. I'm sure that you remember that at one point Banja Luka CSB -- or, rather, Mr. Zupljanin appointed Mr. Radulovic, was temporarily appointed the chief of SJB in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I think there were some other people who got different positions in the Teslic station. I think Milenko Savic became head of the crime department, and Mr. Kos, the uniformed police department. So people from Banja Luka took over after the arrest, some of the positions in the SJB in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: One of the first or maybe even most important roles of this group of people including Mr. Radulovic, was to collect evidence, to carry out investigative steps necessary to process the group the Mices?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that was their main task. And to, of course, make sure that the SJB starts functioning again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And once the Mices were arrested and the situation was stabilised, then this Banja Luka group went back, left Teslic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the period when people from Banja Luka were there, all Muslims and Croats that were in detention at different locations were released with the exception of several against whom indictments were issued and they were still being prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think all of the detention units were disbanded. I don't think anyone remained in any of these facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Following the arrival of Mices, there weren't any large-scale arrests of Croats and Muslims, at least in comparison to the period of Mices?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that there were any after the period of Mices, I mean, arrests of Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I made a little pause, a short pause, because of the transcript. One more question related to this report: Based on this report, you saw and processed -- I can see that quite a lot of evidence was collected that the pre-indictment proceeding was done comprehensively, producing material that was very good for further processing, namely, that the CSB Banja Luka people have done a good job?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was done really well. I have received all the information necessary to issue an indictment and start investigation. There's enough data on those who were victims who are possible witnesses and so on. In other words, I have no complaints in regards to the way the police has prepared the criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It may have been entered wrong into the transcript. I said that there weren't any arrests of Muslims and Croats in the period after the arrest of Mices. So can you confirm that I said "after the arrest of Mices"?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I, in my answer, said that immediately after the arrest of Mices there were no arrests made by the people who had come from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And while that group from Banja Luka was at the station, you had good cooperation with them, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you must know that at one point in time, after these people departed from Banja Luka and when the new chief was appointed, problems arose because the previous leadership using this dual power and miscommunication between authorities basically didn't want to hand over the police station to the new leadership; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those tensions and misunderstandings continued for a long time, as far as I can remember. And there constantly was a latent conflict between Perisic, Markovic, Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Which must have affected the work of police and the efficiency of their work. It affected the efficiency of their work?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably had some consequences. The new chief was also a member of the Crisis Staff, so most likely he was under pressure too. And I don't think that he had worked in the police previously, so that that situation of his was also problematic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, you spoke a lot, both in examination-in-chief and in cross-examination, about certain events in Teslic. So I will now simply go through the report of yours shown to me by the Prosecutor. This is your tab - in the Prosecutor's binder - 84, which is 65 ter 872. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will read to you the second paragraph, which I believe is with the words "The types of crime ..." And it says here that the period of the report coincides with the period of the declared imminent state of war -- imminent threat of war and state of war in the territory of municipality, in certain areas of the municipality. These circumstances and general mobilisation had a considerable impact on the change in the structure of crime in terms of both the types of criminal acts and perpetrators. Actually, as far as I can understand your report, when the armed conflict erupted all of a sudden there emerged a large number of armed persons, which significantly changed the type of crimes committed. That's what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I looked at this report of yours. Please take a look at page 3 where you speak about perpetrators of crimes. And you say, in the first paragraph on page 3 of the B/C/S version, which in English is the same. You say: The public prosecutor and the president of the courts were personally sought at the command of the Teslic Brigade that a person suspected of being an accomplice in murder be released. And then in the next paragraph, where you speak about the destruction of religious facilities, and you say that it needs to be qualified as a war crime. And then you go on to say: "An answer to this question should be sought from the command of the Teslic Serbian Brigade and the Ministry of Interior. Otherwise, people will have an impression that this -- these crimes in the army ranks are tolerated and that no one is trying to prevent it, while the Ministry of Interior will be placed in an unenviable professional situation." As I read it, your main complaint about the crimes committed pertains to the army.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the greatest problem. The army did not organisation the military police, and it did nothing to exert control over the armed persons while those people were not at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this lack of discipline, as you say, caused the Ministry of Interior to be in an unenviable professional situation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes correct. They couldn't really control the situation without cooperating with the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then you go further on to recommend in the next paragraph the following: "To analyse the situation at the level of the corps urgently and take measures to overcome existing weaknesses." So you highlighted the problem and you sought to solve it. You looked at the -- as is the role of the prosecutor, you followed certain criminal phenomena in society and then, as your role is to uncover and prosecute crimes, you also pointed to causes. Because it's not just the police and the prosecutor's office who can effect and bring about the reduction of crime rate. Other organs and institutions need to get involved. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The entire system needs to be involved. It's not just a matter for the police and military police. This needs to be at the level -- this needs to be resolved at the level of the entire system, by having police and the army and everybody else cooperate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what I can see here, in your report -- or, rather, in this information, the main emphasis in highlighting perpetrators again relates to the members of their army, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in this period of time, from June to September that the report covers -- please go back to page 1 of this report. In the last paragraph, under 1, you say: "Relations between the public prosecutor's office and the public security station were good and professional, although they were marked by subjective organisational weaknesses during one period of time." When speaking of this period of time, you are referring to the time when the Mices were in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the period I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then in the period after that, covered by your report, their relations were good?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Concerning those criminal reports that arrived, the cooperation with regard to them was good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, it wasn't just you who observed this problem. The problem was evident. Please look at 85, which is 65 ter 870. This is a request of the army, specifically of the Serbian Teslic Brigade. We received this from the Prosecutor. And there they speak about omissions or failures. They speak about the request of the Teslic Brigade. And in paragraph 1 they elaborate on the same issue that you mentioned in your report. And they say: We shall now list several failures on the part of the command and the commander as the person most responsible for the situation in the brigade. And under 1 they say: The unresolved issue of the military police, which comprises criminals, who are doing everything else but what they're supposed to do. They break into apartments, they bring in people for questioning without arrest warrants, they loot, assault young girls, and beat up soldiers for no reason at all. And so on. Not a single case of crime among the troops (robbery, attempted rape, people forcibly taken from their homes, and the like) has been solved or investigated so far, which was the duty of the military police. Despite all requests to stop the plunder of property in the liberated Croatian and Muslim villages, nothing has been done. This, in fact, reflects the situation that you spoke of yesterday and that you wrote in your report.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of this is correct. I can assure you that the situation was very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And I think that in your interview you mentioned, when it comes to this bringing in without arrest warrants, that you and the president of the court, together, insisted with the command to abolish this prison in Pribinic precisely for these reasons.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then, under item 3, they say: How come the members of the Mice Group received constant support when it is well-known what they had done in Teslic? Mr. Peric, at one point in time when the combat started, the Mice Group or some members of that Group appeared in the region as part of the military police in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard, that some of these men appeared in the Teslic area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when speaking of the strength of the brigade, we can see that, under item 7, the brigade had some 6.500 [as interpreted] men, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that figure mentioned, but it's a factual issue, and I'm not sure that there were indeed as many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As it is mentioned in this information, at the front line there were two and a half thousand soldiers, but the other number is how many had been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never really talked about how many had been at the front line. They were pretty unruly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And there were no clear records, and a large number of these people wore uniforms. It was very difficult to identify who belonged to whom, whether they belonged to the Brigade or not; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Anybody could have worn uniforms or bear arms. What was comprehensible to me was that people were allowed to go on leave with their weapons and that they were allowed to shoot while on leave and so on and nobody thought it was a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the brigade and the command itself did nothing to introduce some order, despite all other efforts and despite your report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the command, not even the Crisis Staff on the board of which the commander of the brigade was. So everybody knew that nobody did nothing, either the commander or civilian authorities, and that was something that caused grave concern due to which I wrote this report and suggested that there needed to be a discussion of these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we ask that this document be admitted, unless it has already been admitted as part of the package. All right. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, another topic that concerns the Mices. While being proofed for this testimony, you had occasion to look at the criminal report and the entire file shown to you yesterday by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. I need to find this file.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. That's tab 14 in your binder. In fact, this criminal report, as far as I could understand, was filed against 16 persons; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you look at page 10 in your version, you can see the actual criminal report. These persons are listed here, so I won't cover them in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the record, this is Exhibit P1363.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said to the Prosecutor -- please look at page 4 of this criminal report, 021 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If can you see this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is P1363; 0211-1713 is the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And here, at page 4 of the criminal report, they say that all of those persons wore camouflage military uniforms and they were armed with short rifles. And then under 7 is Savic Milan, a person who was on the run. In this criminal report they also provide information about other persons who were not available, and they mentioned that Savic was on the run, that the SJB from Teslic and the prosecutor's office couldn't get a hold of him. So this is the OTP binder, tab 14. Please look at the criminal report, which is part of this entire file, and please look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the criminal report. I have a record of statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look at page 10. What I'm trying to show you is on page 10.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 10 is an Official Note from the 13th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know ... look at the ERN number in the right top corner. 0211-7013.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, that's what it says here. All those reported were dressed in camouflage military uniforms, carrying pistols and rifles, a group of reported persons one to seven led by one person who is currently a fugitive, Milan Savic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when the prosecutor asked you why Savic did not feature in this case, the answer is, I think, that he was a fugitive at the moment and he was not accessible to the prosecution organs?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was not arrested because they didn't find him in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But he is covered in this report, and his role is explained. It's just that he could not be found at the moment?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will now move to a different subject, so, perhaps, if you would like to take the break now, or should I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please continue. It's only 12.04.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Ah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Peric, if you look at this criminal report - and I need not remind you because you were the one who wrote it basically - you will see that the gist of this report and the criminal acts enumerated, apart from this first passage which refers to false pretenses and presenting forged identification papers. It says that these persons were not actually employed by the police. And apart from false pretenses, all the other criminal acts are against Muslims and Croats, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The greatest majority, the overwhelming majority of crimes were under Muslims and Croats, although there were some Serbs victims in the injured parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The only one I could see was breaking and entering into a house, this Stanic or Savic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That was the only crime against a Serb?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it was not covered entirely by this report, but there were other cases. There was talk of other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I was not clear enough. The only case of a crime against a Serb covered by the report is this breaking and entering into the Stanic house?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the crimes listed here are primarily related to unlawful detention of a large number of Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is one of the legal qualifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Robbery and robbery/theft against Muslims and Croats; it's another legal qualification mentioned here. If it's easier for you, you can find the description of the crime lower on the page, paragraph in the middle and paragraphs 1, 2, 3, 4, giving the description of these wrong-doings. I'm sorry that this copy we currently have is so bad. Could you just confirm --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot make out all of the text. It's very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 from the top says: "According to a list of rich citizens of Teslic made earlier, persons of exclusively Muslim and Croat ethnicity, the persons reported herewith extorted and robbed citizens, broke and entered into houses, unlawfully detained a large number of citizens, mistreated and physically abused their detainees, explaining that whatever they were doing they were doing in the interests of the Serbian Army and in the interest of establishing a more efficient defence system." Were you able to follow what I was reading?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the text goes on to mention these detention facilities where these people were detained and tortured. And in paragraph 2 -- or, rather, item 2, in the latter part, it says that these people were brought in without any records being made. It mentions physical abuse that resulted in the death of 11 persons. Do you agree that this is in the criminal report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I apologise to you and to everybody else. I was confusing the time we rise with the time we resume. So it is time for a break. So we resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, we will now take a break. In the meantime, would you kindly look at this document, including the next page, because I will have questions relating to that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before you begin, Mr. Krgovic, we just wish to acknowledge the receipt of the batting order from the Office of the Prosecution, for which we thank them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've just taken me by surprise, Your Honour, because I hadn't realised you'd been given it. It hope it's the revised one, which should have just one witness for all of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we've been alerted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, can you hear me? Did you have an opportunity to look at this criminal report during the break?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The copy is bad, but I was able to see what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Basically, among the crimes, you have beatings and unlawful arrest and then the beating up ending in the death of 11 people. On the next page, there is the crime of removal of a number of people. That's on page 5 and paragraph 5 as well. Which states that they were taken to an unknown location and that more than 30 people were killed that had been imprisoned on the premises of the Teslic SJB. In addition to that, it says that they had committed a crime of murdering Hajrudin Becirevic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, there is also mentioned here of the circumstances of their arrest and how the death of a person occurred during the arrest. If you can be of help, when we speak about elements of crime here, in this report it says that they are reported for the crimes as stated therein and appropriate qualifications were provided in line with the regulations in force. When a prosecutor refers a criminal report, you, as I can see here, immediately or actually virtually re-wrote this criminal investigation and put in a request for investigation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the preliminary qualification. The proper qualification comes after investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That means that this initial qualification is not binding on the prosecution and the court? Proper qualification should be carried out after investigation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Proper qualification follows the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you compare these criminal offences listed here and if you look at the crucial elements of the crime, you will agree with me, won't you, that some of them can be categorised, as you said in your report, as war crimes. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that some of these crimes can certainly be qualified as war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And now, these crimes committed in this way and under such circumstances are being tried in Bosnia and Herzegovina as war crimes based on this type of reports?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These kind of crimes are being prosecuted by the BH court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And some of those crimes are based on this and similar reports; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on similar reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the prosecutor is not bound to acknowledge the qualification of the crime provided by those who filed a report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And, on the other hand, the court is not bound by the qualification provided by the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When we speak about filing criminal reports and the issue of jurisdiction, the prosecutor and the investigating court also does not rely on jurisdiction contained in the report. They can always defer this to the competent prosecutor or the competent court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And inasmuch as I was able to understand your testimony, in July 1992, although among these persons were members of the military, a separate group of military personnel, you prosecuted these people precisely because they were linked with the perpetrators who were not members of the military.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We actually applied jurisdiction that we had on all perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Since there was no objection by the defence or by the perpetrators, you continued these proceedings ex officio?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in the event of an objection to the territorial jurisdiction, you should have declared your substantive jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that would fall under the jurisdiction of the military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I was talking about substantive jurisdiction; whereas, in the transcript, it says territorial jurisdiction. You will agree with me that we are talking here about substantive jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing: I can see in this file that there were some supplemental information provided and that after the file had been -- after the report had been filed by the police, they provided some additional statements. Can you find them?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I remember these supplemental -- this supplemental information. I think that these -- this information referred to the injured parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Because there was no time for a number of injured parties to hear within such a sort period of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, while writing this criminal report, you received a thorough and detailed case file which was processed in a proper manner?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Which facilitated your conduct of the proceedings; right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, are you familiar with the fact, apart from what you saw in the file, that these Muslims and Croats who were detained made statements in which they spoke of -- about how they had been armed? It contained certain information about illegal provision of weapons, although that was not the subject of the interest of people who took the statement but that was just mentioned in passing. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. It is possible that we spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if can you find it. There are a few statements that speak about the arming, but I cannot find them at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak slowly and repeat the ERN number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic. Mr. Krgovic, you were asked by the interpreters if you would be good enough to repeat the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0211-7148. That's ERN number from Exhibit P1363.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that this is Emin Rizvanovic's statement. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's marked as attachment 33.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the second sentence in this statement where he says that he hadn't taken part in any military and paramilitary formations. He been brought in because of a semi-automatic rifle that he acquired before the outbreak?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are kindly asking the speakers not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that this issue of arming was just mentioned in passing because that was not the principal subject.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, you spoke today, in response to Mr. Cvijetic's question and also the Prosecutor's question, you spoke about certain proceedings and criminal reports filed in Teslic in 1992. And the Prosecutor showed you the log-book containing these criminal reports. However, I'd like to show you a number of criminal reports that basically confirm what you said to the effect that the majority of these crimes were committed by uniformed personnel. Can you please look at tab 1D, provided to you by Mr. Cvijetic, I'm going to try, although some of those documents haven't been translated, I'll just go briefly through each of them just for you to confirm to me the identity of the person and the crime to which the report refers. So please look at the tab number 6. Actually, it's the list provided by Mr. Cvijetic, 1D, and the exhibit is under tab 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for transcript, it's 1D01-0303. We have a translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a criminal report filed in August 1992 against a Serb, a reserve police officer, who had attempted to steal a car from a Muslim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And he also seised a number of belongings from that person. Do you remember this criminal report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't. I don't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look at this handwritten number which is KI --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a number from your log-book.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure that it has been recorded in the log-book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D00075. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, can we please turn next page - tab 27 - and that's 1D03-2621. It's a criminal report from September, comprising four individuals; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just give me time to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's in tab 7.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 7?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four individuals?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Stanko Marjanovic, Dragan Toprek, Zoran Kolobaric, and Mladen Markovic, and I can see that they're all Serbs. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What I find interesting is that this criminal report was filed - and you can find that on the last page, which is page 5 - by the police, which is to say, by the chief of police station, Jokic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was filed by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And basically this refers to members of the military. All of these persons were members of the military. If you look at number 1, it's a reserve soldier in the 9th Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they were all soldiers. According to the report, they were all deserters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you look at page 2, and when you look at the description of the criminal offence, line 5 from the top, on page 2, you can see that they all were dressed in military uniform. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And they all had military-issue weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you look who the injured party was, you can see -- I think it's -- it's on line 20, was Meho Hamidovic, aka Smajo, and that actually he -- they killed him. So this criminal offence was qualified as murder. It's line 19; you can see who the victim is. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, on page 3 of the same criminal report, where events of the 27th of August are described, where the criminal offence was carried out and the victims were Zukic and his son, both of them Muslims.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the description, in addition to robbing them, they also fired and injured one of the two and after that robbed him. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the very same day, they threatened the injured party Smajo Hamidovic and took some of his property that was in his house.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On page 4, please look at the description of the criminal offence. Again, in this hamlet where the Hamidovics lived, they committed an offence where the injured party was Hamidovic, Hamid; again a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would like to tender this document into evidence. I think that the translation is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D00076.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, I would like to ask you to take a look at a document that's under tab 8 in the binder that you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's 1D00-6709.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As we can see here, Mr. Peric, this is another criminal report. Please take a look at the following page, again signed by the chief of the station, Radomir Jokic.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's a report against four persons again. And, as far as can I see, all four of them are members of the army.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I misled you. Person under number 3 is not a soldier; it's a lady. It's Natasa Petkovic. All the men are members of the army, and the offence was against Muharem Demir, who is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D00077. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I have a problem finding it. You said it's tab number -- I can't remember. But in tab number 8 in -- in -- in your binder, in the binder of Mr. Cvijetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in Mr. Cvijetic's binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab 8 you say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if it helps, it's also in the KT book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Although not with the details, because we went through this yesterday. It's number 166 in the KT book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I found it now. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me show you the following document in Mr. Cvijetic's binder, under tab 9. This is a report that accompanied the criminal report against Kolobaric, Zoran; Markovic, Mladen; and Toprek, Dragan who again dressed in military uniforms, opened fire, and issued threats to the citizens of the village of Gornji Ruzevic, especially Meho Todorovic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It's 1D03-1268.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The village of Gornji Ruzevici was a Muslim-inhabited village?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And these are the individuals that, based on a the previous criminal report, we established have been members of the army?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to submit or tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, Radomir Jokic is again the person who signed the criminal report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the chief of the station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, can I just ask you the purpose of tendering these documents. Is that to show that the public prosecutor in Teslic was actually filing criminal reports concerning perpetrators who belonged to the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this whole line of questioning of this witness -- and this is something I want to get a confirmation of, that this whole series of crimes in Teslic were committed by the army. And we can see here in the absence -- because army wasn't doing anything or taking any measures to prosecute such perpetrators. In cases where it was possible, and witness did explain that to us, it was the police who tried to bring charges, to file criminal reports, and to start the investigation. You will see later on, when we follow the history of these crimes, we will see that they were transferred to other instances, probably because jurisdiction change occurred. I would just like to have the witness confirm events in the relevant period for which he submitted a report between July and September 1992, so that -- so that we would have not only his agreement to my propositions but also evidence that would corroborate it. The Prosecutor submitted or tendered the log-book, and now I'm illustrating it by these criminal reports. There is a larger number of criminal reports than the number the witness calculated using the log-books.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry. We're conflating two slightly different things here. The ones that Mr. Krgovic has gone through are the ones that I draw the witness's attention to yesterday when I was dealing with them as entries in the log-books because we didn't have translations which the Defence have provided. But there are two different things: One, is how many Serbs were prosecuted for crimes against non-Serbs, which was the purpose of our leading that evidence. Whether they're army or not is something that Mr. Krgovic wants to bring up. But I'm not quite clear what other point Mr. Krgovic says he's making by this. Because these are accepted. Where the Prosecution -- Mr. Krgovic is saying that there are others which were not translated. That's another matter. Perhaps he can take him straight -- straight to those ones which we say -- which he says we've missed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, what I'm trying to show: In addition to reports, there were documents accompanying them. In order to be sure when Mr. Peric is speaking about the number of people who were reported in criminal reports, what we can do by examining criminal reports we can see the number of offences and perpetrators. So this will -- this will enable us to see the offences, the identity of perpetrators, and identity of the injure parties. And you will see that in all of the cases we have crimes committed by Serbs against Muslims. If the Prosecution is willing to stipulate that, I can just give you a list of the criminal reports and their numbers. If -- if that's not a contentious issue, we can do it like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Inasmuch as it would be physically impossible to list all of the reports that -- that exist, I assume that there were -- that you selected a representative number that you sought to tender.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I don't think so. There aren't -- that's our case. And if Mr. Krgovic says we're wrong, then can he show us, but our case is there are not hundreds of reports and no representative samples.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor is right. This is only the materials that I have. Of course, that does not mean that I will not find further evidence. We are in the middle an ongoing investigation. We are trying to find whether there are criminal reports in military prosecutor's office. But, at the moment, what I'm trying to do is to tender these documents to show who the perpetrators were, what their identity is, and to confirm - and this is my main point - to confirm something that Mr. Peric already said. Namely, that majority of such crimes were committed by soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You seemed open to the suggestion that was put forward a little earlier about stipulation in this regard, if the Prosecution doesn't resist it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if -- as I say, we went through all -- Judge Peric went through the books to check. The simple question was, What cases -- prosecutions during the relevant period were there of Serbs for offences committed against non-Serbs. He came up with that list which we went through at some speed yesterday. I understand the suggestion from the Defence is that we may be wrong. If they show, though, the other entries in the records to us and it's quite clear that we were wrong, then we'll make that concession. But I -- I don't know exactly -- as I say, the point that Mr. Krgovic is trying to make, if it's simply that, then that's something we can look at. If it's more than that, well, then, he may want to go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to -- to my learned friend. It is just a minor correction to the transcript, Your Honours. It's page 61, line -- between line 4 and 8. The word used in the transcript regarding the jurisdiction was "substantive jurisdiction." I think the more appropriate word is, in legal terms, is "subject matter jurisdiction." So it should be just taken like that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We understood that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I was under the impression that there was some sort of consensus between the parties that albeit that most of the cases that had been entered in the log-book, the KT log-book, were cases concerning crimes committed by Serbs against Serbs, a few of those cases did, in fact, concern crimes committed by Serbs against non-Serbs. And then I thought that your point that you have been bringing up today was that the military prosecutor didn't function properly; that's why the civilian or the public prosecutor had to do the job. And so the question of the Chamber is, if you could elicit from the witness now, whether it would be up for the public prosecutor anyway to start the investigation and then, if it turned out that the perpetrator belonged to the army, then hand over the case to the army. And if the witness answers positively to this question, the next question would then be: How many of the cases that you have now shown us were actually handed over to the military prosecutor? Is this a correct perception of the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have heard Judge Harhoff's question. Can you please answer it.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, of course, it was essential to first determine the facts so that one could determine whose jurisdiction it was. So police was required to go through the investigative stage, and only then the prosecutor could make a decision concerning the jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The prosecutor could do one of the two things upon seeing that it's not under his jurisdiction: To transfer the criminal report to the relevant military prosecutor. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He could have done that. Or first start an investigation and then transfer the case after the investigation. And, thirdly, was the court who have transferred the case. The jurisdiction is an issue that can be determined in the course of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Based on this, you accepted some of the criminal reports and acted upon them?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We received the reports, collected evidence, and then, later on, decisions were made about jurisdiction. The log-book will show what was transferred to the military prosecutor's office at what stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. But also, certain number of the criminal reports were submitted to the military prosecutor's office but through you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that some reports were transferred to the military prosecution. We've seen from one report that three persons were in a military detention facility. So in cases like that, we probably transferred the report, the criminal report, to the military prosecutor because they were already in remand in their prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. I'll show you several criminal reports of that kind. They are in the binder that's before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you would allow me to continue with this document, I have maybe four or five criminal reports here -- or, rather, there's more. I think there's six of them that cover the type of cases we've been discussing. So we have here reports against members of the army. Then we have a report to the military prosecutor but through the log-book from Teslic, which were then transferred to the military prosecutor's office in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Six, you say? Please proceed. It seems that the shortest way would be to have these exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, please find under 14. It's 1D03-1256. It's a criminal report by the SJB Teslic that was submitted to the Military Prosecutor Office in Bijeljina. It's your K number 177 -- your KI number 177. Again, signed by the chief of the station Radomir Jokic. This criminal report is against seven individuals. Individuals under numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 are all members of the army. And numbers 6 and 7 are civilians. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see that in the report. But what is not clear to me is how this can be a criminal report by the prosecutor office in Teslic. It was transferred to Bijeljina. I'm not sure about this KU number 177.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this 177 number seems to indicate it went through your log-book.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. At least it shouldn't have. It could be the log-book of the Military Prosecutor's Office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That means, Mr. Peric, that this criminal report, under number 14 and the criminal report under tab 15 -- could you look at that? It's 1D03-1625.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Again, the Military Prosecutor's Office. It was transferred to them.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not through the prosecutor's office in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It went directly to the Military Prosecutor's Office, and these two do not fall under the number you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just confirm, therefore, so I can get this straight, if that's all right. These do not -- these cases do not appear in the KT log-book then?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You see from these two reports that the persons were members of the Teslic Brigade. Look at this document in tab 14. You mentioned that there were Muslims included in one group of perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I know that there was a military unit, including Muslim members, in the area of Pelagicevo in the Posavina area, so it could have gone to the military court in Bijeljina and that the members of that military unit were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The reason I'm showing you this -- look at page 2, item 14 -- tab 14, sorry. You will see that there -- where this Kolobaric, Stanko, Mladic, and another person -- it's just another part of the group that was reported in your area?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possibly members of the same group but a different incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This crime was against Muslims from Osivica village, from what I see.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Teslic municipality.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know if I established enough link in order to have this document admitted, because these persons are related, associated with one another. Perhaps the document can be admitted if there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not objecting, Your Honours, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 1D03-1268 shall be Exhibit 2D00078. Document tab 1D03-1256 shall be Exhibit 2D00079. While document ID03-1625 shall be Exhibit 2D00080. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look also at the next document under tab 15; the numbers at the end are 1625. These persons were reported, Jovicic Miodrag and another person, concerning an incident in the Teslic. In the vicinity of the health centre they shot at this Muslim, trying to kill him. A person by the name of Halilovic. It was reported to the Military Prosecutor's Office. Do you remember such incidents in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think -- I think that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Again, army personnel is involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I tender this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 2D00081. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, you mentioned during examination-in-chief about those criminal reports against unidentified perpetrators. I would like to show you two criminal reports against unidentified perpetrators, indicated in the original as NN perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel tell us the number a bit faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's tab 12. 1D03-1275.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a criminal report against an unidentified perpetrator, and it's about racketeering against a family of Muslims in Osivica village. Sorry. Firing from -- firing rockets -- firing rockets against a family house belonging to a Muslim family.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's from a hand-held rocket-launcher called Zolja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If you look further, you will see that the police came out of the crime scene and that it was established that from a distance of 80 metres from the Mahmutovic house projectiles were fired from a hand-held launcher, Zolja. As far as I know, this is a weapon currently in the arsenal of the army in the Teslic area.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was an army weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you look at the next document, 1D03-1272, tab 13, you will see that these incidents happened within a sort span of time. And, again, rockets were fired against a family house belonging to Muslims.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And I suppose it's the same weapon. A rocket-launcher is mentioned. And the perpetrators were probably soldiers. These things happened in Teslic at the time.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe the incidents of these crimes was quite high.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that you will agree in prosecuting such crimes it was rather difficult if the victim had no direct contact with the perpetrator. If a rocket was fired from a certain distance, it was difficult to identify the perpetrators beyond suspecting that they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. It was very difficult. You could only suppose this could have been done by people outside of the army, because sometimes these weapons were in the hands of civilians, not only army personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we assign exhibit numbers to these two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. I think the previous document, 1D03-1625, has been assigned two -- yeah, two numbers. 80 and 81. So I think that the next one has to be 81. 1D1275 has to be number 81.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. 1D03-1275 shall be Exhibit 2D00081, while 1D03-1272 shall be begin Exhibit 2D00083. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I just want to correct that. 1D03-1275 shall be Exhibit 2D00081. While 1D03-1272 shall be Exhibit 2D00082. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Peric, with regard to unidentified perpetrators, I will show you a document that relates the efforts of the police to deal with such things. And now, in my binder, would you look at the last document, number 14. It's 1D00-2248. Not the binder shown to you by Mr. Cvijetic, but my binder. While the employees of the CSB were trying to restore order, I don't suppose that there were any complaints from you or the citizens to the work of the station?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember any complaints.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You will see a letter sent to crime investigation services. I don't know if the chief of the sector informed you of this; Djuro Bulic was the chief of the sector in the Banja Luka centre?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The CSB is requesting information from public security stations in the region, more specifically from crime investigation departments. It is addressed to chiefs. And he requests that -- not later, that 22nd November, 1992, they provide information related to all serious crimes which occurred on their territory starting with January 1, 1991, and referring to unidentified perpetrators. Crimes belonging within the jurisdiction of the crime investigation service are listed; killing, aggravated robbery, drug trafficking, crimes perpetrated by police employees, explosions, sabotage, business crime, white-collar crime, and other serious crimes, in brackets we see war crimes and such, committed, we repeat, by unidentified perpetrators. Mr. Peric, this appears to be an effort by the Security Services Centre to deal with this problem of crimes reported against unidentified perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can interpret it as such. I don't know what the real purpose was, but, on the face of it, it seems so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the last-but-one paragraph. It says: "We need this to get a true picture of crime incidents in the region in order to organise assistance from the level of the Crime Investigation Service of the CSB." In essence, the CSB where Stojan Zupljanin is working is requesting this information to identify the problem and to do the same thing that was done in Teslic in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may interpret it in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding your experience with the CSB Banja Luka --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, if something is funny, that you share with us so that we could also -- is there any particular reason why you are laughing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, I apologise for this interruption. Just one question: What is your experience of Stojan Zupljanin's reaction and work regarding incidents involving unidentified perpetrators? Is it your experience that he tried to deal with this problem in the same way as indicated in this dispatch, to try to help deal with the problem?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could be interpreted in this -- in that way, but I don't know what the real approach and attitude of Stojan Zupljanin and the CSB was regarding the station in Teslic. I cannot say with any certainty one way or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in these meetings you had at municipal level together with MUP representatives, do you know that such requests were made, that they reached the Teslic CSB -- sorry, public security station?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. But I know that if it were not from Predrag Radulovic who came from Teslic originally, who knew the situation well, I doubt very much that anything would have been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Because essentially the problem in Teslic was that all the power was concentrated at municipal level. It was a closed system.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I believe the Crisis Staff had all the power and made all the key decision. But I don't know how -- how they related to the supreme, the highest authorities, what the relationship was with local authorities. I don't know what the attitude and approach of Stojan Zupljanin was to the local structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that precisely because of these and similar events in Teslic the leadership of the public security station in Teslic was replaced for failing to deal with it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's true that they were replaced, but they later returned in the same composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: There was a problem of jurisdiction between Doboj and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There must have been organisational problems that I know next to nothing about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in conclusion, Teslic finally went to the Doboj jurisdiction, and it's still there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Zupljanin and Bjelosevic were or the same level in the structure. I don't know what the relationship was between Teslic and Doboj. It's -- it's rather blurry, that situation, at least from my perspective.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But administratively speaking, as far as the police is concerned and the courts are concerned, Teslic belongs to this day to the Doboj region?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those two jurisdiction only. All the other administrative jurisdiction fell within Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me show you just one more criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 1D03-1316.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your tab 19. You see, it's a criminal report filed in 1993. But if you look at the second page carefully, you will see that it concerns crimes committed in 1992.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Nedjeljko Vukovic, named here, is a civilian; Rajko Trifunovic, 2nd lieutenant; Mile Arsenic, reservist with the 1st Battalion; and Grujo Lazic, also reservist, with the 10th Battalion. The crimes concerned were committed against Hamdija Potic [phoen], Mehmed Ranic [phoen], Franjo Cosic [phoen], Kaja Cosic [phoen], all of them Muslims or Croats?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It was filed with the Teslic prosecutor office. It was filed in 1993 but concerns 1992.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It straddles 1992 and 1993, that is, end January 1993. It is a crime of theft obviously lasting for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the proceedings were ongoing before a Military Prosecutor's Office, regardless of this report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO PERIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I request a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D00083.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I planned to embark upon a new, albeit short, subject and show a new exhibit to the witness, but I believe it's time to adjourn now. My examination so far went rather more slowly than I expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, in terms of the time that you had indicated that you would be with this witness, when we resume tomorrow, you would have four minutes left. I don't know how you -- you said that you have a short matter, so you would bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have another 20 minutes of examination left. I hope you will indulge me. Administrative matters took up quite a while, and Mr. Cvijetic also has some time left. I believe we still keep to the limit of time allocated for our examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
